desc:
You are given a palindrome s of lowercase letters. Replace exactly one character with any lowercase letter so that the new string is not a palindrome, and make the new string the lexicographically smallest one possible.

Return that string. If it is impossible to make s a non-palindrome with one replacement, return the single character -.

"abccba"  -> "aaccba"
"aaa"     -> "aab"
"a"       -> "-"
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: A string of length 1 is always a palindrome. What about every longer palindrome - can you always break it?
To make the result small you want to lower an early character, ideally to a. But the change must actually destroy the symmetry.

Look at the first half only (not the middle character of an odd-length string, since changing it never breaks a palindrome). The first character there that is not a becomes a. If every character in the first half is already a, change the last character to b.
editorial: Changing the middle letter of an odd palindrome keeps it a palindrome, so only the positions in the first half and their mirrors are useful. A change at index i in the first half breaks the palindrome as long as the new letter differs from its mirror s[n-1-i].

To get the smallest result, change the leftmost position where a decrease is possible. In the first half, the first letter that is not a can be lowered to a, and the mirror still holds the old, non-a letter, so the string is no longer a palindrome. If the whole first half consists of as, then (as the string is a palindrome) the whole string is as apart from possibly the middle. No decrease is possible, so the smallest legal change is to raise the very last character to b, which makes the string larger as late as possible. Length 1 has no valid change.
One pass over half the string: O(n) time.
